## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rūpavibhatti* ("Analysis of Corporeality") is a section of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [U Kyaw Khine 1999]. It forms the detailed exposition (B: Exposition in Detail) of the *Rūpakaṇḍa*, which constitutes part II of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* and is recognized as having formed an originally separate text equipped with its own *mātikā* [von Hinüber 1996; U Kyaw Khine 1999]. The commentary on the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (*Aṭṭhasālinī*) similarly recognizes this textual division under the title *Rūpavibhatti* alongside *Cittavibhatti* and *Nikkheparāsi* [von Hinüber 1996].

Methodologically, rather than providing a direct singular enumeration of all material phenomena (*rūpa-dhammā*), the *Rūpavibhatti* unfolds their definitions and implications through an extensive series of classifications structured into ten sections arranged in ascending numerical order [Karunadasa 1967]. It opens with corporeality viewed as a single category (*ekaka-naya*), followed by dyadic sets where the first section alone encompasses one hundred and four two-group classifications, the last ninety of which are developed systematically [Karunadasa 1967; U Kyaw Khine 1999].
